featured_reviews.name: Suhas Kulkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Exceptionally Great Breakfast experience for us at this restaurant!

Very neat and tidy but clean place, with only four tables on the ground floor and probably another four on the first floor. Very simple interior and ambience that makes us feel at ease.

Very good service by a very efficient person Tiwari ji who is always on the move and taking care of every person on every table, without a need to call again and remind for anything. A very humble person with smiling face, Tiwari ji caters to all our requests with full energy throughout. He is Occasionally assisted or supported by the owner of the place who supervises all activities, in the kitchen and with the guests alike.

Now, coming to the food part, a really awesome experience I would say.

An humble Upma, tasted so nice, making me to say it was one of the best Upmas I must have eaten outside. Everything was so impeccable with its looks, texture, taste and it was doubly complimented by the Coconut Chutney served alongwith it.

Rasam Vada with Chutney was another great thing to savour, no complaints on it.

The Star of the show was Button Idly with Srilankan Curry -  something I am short of words to appreciate and explain. Sambhar replaced by Coconut based gravy in a bowl and button idlys immersed in them, so that they absorb all the flavours of the gravy within them, each bite of every piece of the Idly kept us craving for more! A very great and unique experience for us.

All this ended with a supurb dose of Filter Coffee, customised to our choice of regular or strong and that really left us super satisfied.

There is no parking available here, one has use the Pay and Parking place of the shopping mall just adjesannt to this place.

Overall, a must visit place if we happen to be in this area anytime. One may need to wait for tables, for its being occupied with people who are in no hurry while enjoying the food here!

featured_reviews.name: Prabinsum
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a company audit done today by me and we posed as customers. Too many complains. Owners can take this as an advise in order to improvise.

1. Don't play music so loud that visitors find it difficult to talk. And if at all music is played don't connect your paytm payment notification tones and phone call rings on the same player. It's really annoying to hear your phone ringtones on speakers and also I'm not interested to know how much my next table person is paying.

2. Put curtains in the ac room. Ac cooling effect will be more and also too much harsh sun light coming inside. It's good if you have greenery outside. There you just have scorching sun. So better cover the glass.

3. When you have sugar packets on the table, then why waiter is asking wether we want with sugar or without sugar. It's improper customer service training. Train the waiters.

4. Make sure the menu has basic things. Being a south Indian Brahmin cafe if you don't have idli, it's not right. You have thatte idli but keep steamed idlis too.

5. Right after bill amount was received, the waiter immediately asked us - "aapka hogaya kya" he din't even wait for a second to ask this question which was unexpected and rude. Again lack of customer service skills. Respect your customers.

6. The staircase is too narrow and I understand. The interiors are nice. Place is well utilised. Hats off to that but when customers are already climbing down and waiter can see it, he should step down, he stood there like a pillar and we had to literally sqeeze and go through him and pass downwards. He should realise manners when there are female customers.

These small and simple things make huge difference. There may be customers who don't bother about all this but even 1% of dissatisfaction should not exist in any business.

Thank you !

featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly, the best South Indian food that I have had till date. Truly authentic, very well made with lots of care.
The Sri Lankan curry with idli and Vada were just awesome, so is the sheera and all the dosas and idlis. But the main attraction and the showstopper was the benne dosa, which was crip from the outside and a bit soft from the inside, topped with amazing chutneys and their perfect sambhar. The filter coffee was also one of the best I have ever had.
The ambience is very attractive with cute cartoon decorations.
A must visit for true South Indian cuisine lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant lad
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a tropical escape right in the heart of Mumbai, Laguna by TGS in Santacruz is a place you need to check out. With its lush tropical vibes, vibrant ambience, and unique concept of a coffee and cocktail bar, Laguna offers the perfect setting whether you’re stopping by for a coffee during the day or unwinding with cocktails in the evening.

We started with a couple of their signature cocktails. The Tamarindo, a tequila-based cocktail, was refreshing with a lovely tangy kick and a well-balanced flavour profile. The Purple Palm, made with gin, was smooth, aromatic, and incredibly easy to sip on.

For appetisers, the Nachos Supreme was easily one of the highlights. The portion was generous and loaded with flavour, making it ideal for sharing with friends. The Buffalo Chicken Wings packed a punch with their spicy and zesty flavours and paired perfectly with the drinks.

For the mains, we tried the Chicago Style Deep Dish Pizza, The Big Greek Pizza. The base had a nice crisp texture and was topped generously, making every slice satisfying and flavourful. We also enjoyed The Nine Mile Bowl, a wholesome vegan dish featuring vegan paneer, rice, salsa, onions, and other fresh elements. It was hearty, comforting, and full of vibrant flavours.

To finish, we had the Burnt Honey and Vanilla Cheesecake. Rich, creamy, and indulgent, it had beautiful caramelised honey notes that made it the perfect dessert to end the meal.

What makes Laguna stand out is how effortlessly it combines a café culture with a vibrant bar experience. Whether you’re a coffee lover, a cocktail enthusiast, or simply looking for a place that feels like a mini tropical getaway in the city, Laguna by TGS delivers a memorable experience with great food, creative drinks, and a lovely atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Ishita Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place in Mumbai that quietly sets the bar ridiculously high for café dining, it has to be Journal.

Tucked in the lanes of Santacruz West, this spot feels like a hidden gem that you almost want to gatekeep — but it’s too good not to talk about.

Let’s start with the food — because wow.
I tried the Rigatoni Romesco pasta, and I’m not exaggerating when I say it has redefined what a good pasta should taste like for me. Perfectly cooked, rich, and balanced — the kind of dish you keep thinking about days later. The grilled artichoke & mushroom pizza was equally incredible — earthy, flavourful, and done just right.

What makes Journal stand out is that the food isn’t just good — it’s consistently thoughtful. The menu spans across multiple healthy and cheat options, so there’s always something exciting to try.  ￼
And nothing feels like filler — even the simplest dishes feel well-crafted.

The space itself adds so much charm to the experience. You’ve got both indoor and outdoor seating, and the outdoor section especially makes for a perfect brunch vibe. It’s relaxed, airy, and yes — there are quite a few cats casually strolling around, which somehow just adds to the whole personality of the place.

The vibe is exactly what you want from a café — calm, slightly buzzy, and very “slow morning energy.” It’s spacious, comfortable, and great whether you’re working, catching up, or just unwinding.  ￼

And the coffee? Absolutely holds its own. Smooth, well-brewed, and clearly taken seriously — which makes sense given it positions itself as a space for “coffee, culture & conversations.”  ￼

featured_reviews.review_text:
**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

To end the meal on a sweet note, we ordered the Hangover Chocolate. It was indulgent, rich, and every chocolate lover's dream—a dessert that lingers on your taste buds long after the meal is over.

Overall, the restaurant scores high on food, service, and ambiance. Whether you're a vegetarian or just someone who loves good food, this place is sure to leave you impressed.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited EVE Santacruz on a Thursday night and honestly the overall vibe of the place was really good. The ambience is beautiful, very lively and aesthetically done, making it a great spot for dinner plans, birthdays, or even a casual night out with friends. Since it was Thursday, they had live music and that completely elevated the experience. The place felt quite happening with good energy, good crowd, and a fun atmosphere throughout the evening.

What I liked most was that despite being crowded, the place still had a comfortable and enjoyable dining feel. The music created a nice balance — entertaining but not too loud to the point where you can’t talk. Service was decent and the staff was polite as well.

Coming to the food, it was okayish according to me. Not bad at all, but the ambience and overall experience definitely stood out more than the food itself. Some dishes were good while some felt average, but the presentation was nice.

Overall, I’d say it’s definitely worth visiting if you enjoy places with good ambience, live music, and vibrant nightlife vibes. Perfect place to unwind and enjoy the atmosphere with your group.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Gogri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paid premium price for a thoroughly mediocre experience, Eve was an absolute disappointment.

The staff seemed poorly trained and completely unprofessional, honestly felt like they had no hospitality background. The entire floor was chaotic, people shouting across sections, and managers constantly rearranging tables to squeeze in more guests. At one point, a table right next to us was given to new customers without even being cleaned.

Basic service etiquette was missing, plates weren’t changed unless we explicitly asked. On top of that, staff would hover right next to the table and the moment you finished a dish or drink, they’d immediately push you to order something else. It felt more like pressure than service.

Coming to the food, extremely underwhelming.
Nachos were the only decent dish. The mango salad had barely 7–8 pieces, the spaghetti was basic and poorly executed. Even classic cocktails like a Manhattan (served in the wrong glass!) and an Espresso Martini were messed up. Only the Picante managed to save some face.

Apart from the staircase with the “library” aesthetic, which is clearly designed for Instagram - there’s nothing special about this place.

For ~₹3,500 per person, this experience was nowhere close to worth it. There are far better restaurants in the city.

Avoid this place if you value your money and experience.

featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

With regard,
Team Nānna House

featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

The service was not just excellent but also remarkably prompt, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable dining experience. Its location, just near the Santacruz local station exit, makes it incredibly easy to access. Nanumal Bhojraj isn't just a restaurant; it's a heartwarming culinary experience that exceeds expectations, proving that exceptional taste and service know no time limits. This place is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic, soulful Indian vegetarian food.

The Green Door Restaurant has a very pleasant ambiance with well-designed interiors, and the food variety and taste are truly commendable. It’s a great place for a relaxed meal and quality dining experience.
However, one area that needs attention is crowd management during kitty parties. While such gatherings are understandable, the noise and disturbances significantly affect other guests who come seeking a peaceful atmosphere and good food.

Overall, a lovely place with great potential to be even better.
